title: Build a deterministic trade validator

objectives.text: Combine record validation, duplicate policy and exact arithmetic without mutating input.
Return an explicit accepted/rejected report whose counts and totals reconcile to the declared policy.
Apply exact ASCII lexical/range checks in declared first-failure order without mutating state.
Commit seen IDs, last valid time, count and exact four-decimal-place notional only after a fully valid record.

blocks.markdown: Build a pure local batch validator, not a trading gateway. Each record must have exactly trade_id, price_cents and quantity_shares. ID is a nonempty string. Price and quantity are exact nonnegative integers, excluding bool. Invalid records are rejected with an index and reason; later records still run. Duplicate IDs are rejected only after an earlier valid record with that ID was accepted. An invalid first appearance does not reserve the ID. Records are not sent anywhere and no trades are placed.

blocks.caption: Expected output: 2; a rejection list with index 1 duplicate and index 2 numeric; then 821. Only accepted records contribute to notional. Indexes in this report are zero-based.

blocks.markdown: After each processed prefix, accepted and rejected counts sum to the number of processed records. seen is exactly the set of accepted IDs. total_cents is the sum of accepted price-times-quantity amounts. These are three separate invariants; checking only the final total can miss a dropped rejection or duplicated accepted record. The reason priority is fields, then ID, then numeric, then duplicate, so a record violating several rules receives the first reason. This is a deliberately stated reporting policy.

This exercise consumes already parsed Python dictionaries. It does not teach CSV framing, quoted fields or reading untrusted gigabyte files. A CSV-parser problem needs its own teaching and input limits. Do not assume a familiar title means every related parsing skill has been covered.

blocks.caption: Expected output: contract checks passed. The tests inspect input preservation, report reconciliation and exact arithmetic separately.

blocks.markdown: Independent transfer: hide the worked solution and implement the validator again from its written specification, then run the same contract checks. Add cases for empty input, a missing field, an extra field, True as quantity, a duplicate valid ID, and an invalid first record followed by a valid record using the same ID. A shallow record copy is enough here because every accepted value is an immutable string or integer; extending the schema with nested mutable data needs a new copying policy.

Write a brief run report: source revision, runtime, tests executed, counts and total, and known exclusions. Do not call this production-ready merely because its examples pass. External persistence, fees, corrections, authentication and real feed formats are outside this local project. The next modules add data handling and more explicit engineering constraints.

Technical references: [Python data structures tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/datastructures.html) for dictionaries and sets; [Python errors tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/errors.html) for explicit input errors. The financial schemas, policies and synthetic cases in this lesson are declared teaching contracts, not claims about a particular venue or employer.

The earlier core uses a different, narrower example. These separate extensions now teach the named exact public contracts, not a silent change to the earlier function. Keep the schemas, rounding rules and parser return shapes distinct. Work through each part and its checks separately.

A distinct literal-comma schema

The current public contract explicitly means ASCII letters and digits, even when non-ASCII text appears. There are up to 30,000 lines of at most 200 characters. Each record is id,symbol,side,qty,price,ts. Split literal commas into exactly six fields. Unlike the separate CSV state-machine exercise, this schema does not enable quoted fields. Do not strip or normalize case.

verdict(line, seen_ids, last_ts) returns an error string or None without changing state. The supplied main still has a TODO for valid-record updates. The complete process_records function below supplies that missing fold; replacing verdict alone would not complete the program.

Nine checks in a fixed order

Run BAD_FIELDS, BAD_ID, BAD_SYMBOL, BAD_SIDE, BAD_QTY, BAD_PRICE, BAD_TS, DUP_ID, then OUT_OF_ORDER. Return the first failure.

ID must match ASCII [A-Za-z0-9]+ and is case-sensitive. Symbol is [A-Z]{1,6}; side is exactly B or S. Quantity is [1-9][0-9]*, at most 10^9. Price has one or more ASCII digits, optionally a point and one to four digits, and must be positive. Integer prices and leading zeros in prices are allowed. Timestamp is 0 or [1-9][0-9]*, at most 10^12. Empty fractions, trailing points, scientific notation, signs, spaces, NaN and infinity are not valid prices.

Lexical checks before conversion and state

Use fullmatch, not prefix matching or permissive float parsing. [0-9] means ASCII digits. Python isdigit/isalnum and regex \d/\w accept more characters, and \w also accepts underscore. Convert numeric text only after its lexical check; short-circuit conditions prevent int on malformed input.

Quantity, price, and timestamp failures all outrank DUP_ID. DUP_ID outranks OUT_OF_ORDER. A duplicated ID with an invalid side reports BAD_SIDE. A duplicated ID with older time but otherwise valid fields reports DUP_ID. Equal timestamps are allowed; only a smaller timestamp is out of order.

Valid-only state invariant

Before each record, seen is exactly the set of earlier accepted IDs; last is the previous accepted timestamp, initially 0; valid is the accepted count; total is the exact accepted qty*price sum in units of 10^-4.

If verdict returns an error, emit it and change nothing. Otherwise emit OK, add the ID, set last, increase valid, and add the product. This single commit boundary preserves the invariant by induction. Rejection must not reserve an ID or move time. An out-of-order record can reuse its ID successfully in a later valid record.

Exact scale and no invented magnitude bound

Parse price as whole*10000 plus its fractional digits right-padded to four places. Multiply by integer quantity, sum accepted products, then format total//10000 and total%10000 padded to four digits. Both B and S contribute positive notional; side is not a sign in this task.

The public price has no magnitude limit beyond the 200-character line. A legal value can exceed both 64 and 128 bits. Python arbitrary-precision integers handle the full contract; do not assume a fixed 64-bit or 128-bit accumulator covers it. Fixed-width C++ remains held unless its implementation supports every legal magnitude. Avoid float, insufficient Decimal context precision, and truncating to cents.

Trace and complete adapter

A,X,B,1,1,5 is accepted: seen={A}, last=5, total=10000. B,X,B,1,1,4 is OUT_OF_ORDER and does not reserve B. B,X,S,2,0.0001,5 is then accepted: last=5, total=10002, valid=2. A,X,Q,1,1,1 reports BAD_SIDE before duplicate or time checks. Final lines are VALID 2 and NOTIONAL 1.0002.

Retain the supplied newline parser and its n-record loop. Fill its TODO with the valid-only updates, not updates after every verdict. process_records returns exactly these verdict and summary lines and demonstrates the complete fold.

Proof, work, and independent transfer

An ordered return proves every preceding check passed. Induction over the commit step proves accepted IDs, last valid time, count, and exact notional. Rejected records cannot affect later validation.

Each line has bounded length 200, but big-integer arithmetic still has a digit cost. Set membership is expected constant time, not an unconditional hashing guarantee. Storage grows with accepted IDs and output. Independently compute all field predicates in order, then fold accepted records with exact Decimal or Fraction arithmetic. Test every field alone and simultaneous failures, Unicode digits/letters, price leading zeros, valid-only ID reuse, case-sensitive IDs, equal timestamps, maximum record count, and huge legal prices. This is local teaching, not production risk or compliance certification.

blocks.caption: Expected ['OK', 'OUT_OF_ORDER', 'OK', 'BAD_SIDE', 'VALID 2', 'NOTIONAL 1.0002'], then BAD_ID. Complete pure verdict function plus a valid-only exact state fold.

summary: A batch report is a contract: accepted/rejected counts reconcile, accepted IDs stay unique, exact notional totals match accepted records and input is preserved. Record known exclusions. Extension: ordered record state fold.
